data.narrative:
Cascade Space is a seed-stage space & aerospace company founded by Jacob Portukalian and Arlen Abraham, having raised $5.9M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 13 private peers (including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs) and 5 public-market anchors (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Only one valuation method proved applicable. The Stage-Progression approach uses total capital raised ($6M proxy) as a baseline and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $15M. Peer-Median anchoring was not viable: while 14 same-sector private peers exist, zero qualified within narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), and a broad-sector median would lack precision. Public-Comp anchoring cannot be applied due to the absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies. The Space & Aerospace public median trades at 26.4x revenue across six tickers, but without Cascade's topline this multiple offers no usable anchor.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M to $17M, centered on $15M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the single stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x step-up multiplier to Cascade's specific market position and the absence of revenue or unit-economics data to cross-check against public comparables or private peer financing rounds.
